decisions.reason: The independence/any-combination assertion is false for the realized forces on admissible states. Fix time, velocities and other positions in a local product box contained in open Q. For r=x_i-x_j != 0, centrality writes F_ij=a r and F_ji=b r (with reversed arguments in F_ji). Although the pair maps are only locally Lipschitz, the pair signature makes F_ij C1 in x_j and F_ji C1 in x_i: all other summands in F_i or F_j are independent of that variable, and F=-grad U is C1. Consequently a is C1 in x_j and b in x_i. Mixed-partial symmetry for C2 U gives D_{x_j}F_ij=(D_{x_i}F_ji)^T. For any nonzero w perpendicular to r, contracting both sides with w yields -a|w|^2=b|w|^2, hence F_ji=-F_ij. At admissible coincident positions, continuity and centrality along different separation directions force both pair values to zero. This argument concerns pair arguments attained by Q, not unused extensions of pair-map domains. Thus separate optional hypotheses do not justify arbitrary logical independence; the repaired status paragraph requires joint consistency without changing any adopted clause.

Adopt, as this page's **impact and open-mass extensions** of the force
branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and [[post-cm02-interactions]],
the following three model extensions. Each is an adopted model, not a
consequence of the smooth-force postulates; each applies only where a
statement explicitly invokes it.

- **Why the extensions are adopted rather than derived.** A motion of the
  smooth-force branch with a continuous force map has a $C^1$ momentum curve
  and no jumps; hence no choice of smooth force maps produces the momentum
  jump of clause 3 with $J\ne0$ at an isolated time. The closed, fixed-label
  smooth-force model does not account for matter crossing a body boundary;
  clause (iii) adopts that additional accounting. Constant body mass alone
  does not exclude exchange: its mass balance permits
  $r_{\mathrm{in}}=r_{\mathrm{out}}>0$, and different entering and leaving
  inertial velocities can give a nonzero momentum flux. The extensions
  enlarge the model class; they are not consequences of
  [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] or [[post-cm02-interactions]], and the
  exact statement that a smooth-force motion cannot jump is proved on this
  page as part of [[pthm-cm15-impact-balance]].

Adopt, as the **central-force model** for the two-body part of this page, the
following restricted model class inside the force and interaction branches of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and [[post-cm02-interactions]].

**(i) The two-label central model.** A model of class (i) is a force model of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=2$ labels, fixed masses
$m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), a time window $I_0$, the
collision-excluded configuration domain
$$Q:=\{\,x=(x_1,x_2)\in(\mathbb R^3)^2:\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert\in J_0\,\}$$
for an open interval $J_0\subseteq(0,\infty)$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]), and the force map presented through the
time-independent **static central pair potential**
$$U(x_1,x_2):=u(\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert),\qquad u:J_0\to\mathbb R\ \text{of class }C^2,$$
so that $F_i(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_i}U(x)$ on the state domain (clauses (iii)
and (iv) of [[post-cm02-interactions]]; $U$ is of class $C^2$ on the open
$Q$ by [[lem-cm05-radial-potential-gradient]]). In the external-plus-pair
presentation of clause (i) of that postulate the model has
$F_i^{\mathrm{ext}}\equiv0$: no external forces act on the labels of a model
of class (i).

- **Why the class is adopted rather than derived.** Centrality, the existence
  of a potential and the absence of external forces are restrictions of the
  force branch, and [[post-cm02-interactions]] records that an arbitrary force
  map need satisfy none of them. This postulate selects the subclass the page
  develops, and every theorem of the page remains conditional on it.

**(a) Potential representation of the force map.** A model **presents its
force map through a potential** when it declares a function
$$U:I_{0}\times Q\longrightarrow\mathbb R$$
of class $C^{2}$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), of
dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (read in joules), with
$$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)\qquad(i=1,\dots,N)$$
for every $(t,x,v)$ of the state domain; here $\nabla_{x_{i}}U$ is the
gradient of $u\mapsto U(t,x_{1},\dots,x_{i-1},u,x_{i+1},\dots,x_{N})$ at
$u=x_{i}$. More generally, a model may declare **residual forces**
$d_{i}:I_{0}\times Q\times(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}\to\mathbb R^{3}$ of the standing
regularity of clause (iii) of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and present
$$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v);$$
the pair $(U,d)$ is then the model's presentation and
$F_{i}^{\mathrm{p}}:=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U$ is its **potential part**. The scalar
$U$ is a **potential energy** for the model's potential part; the framework's
earlier admission of potentials in [[post-cm02-interactions]] clause (iii) is
the special case $d\equiv0$. A model that presents its whole force map this
way with $d\equiv0$ is a **global potential model** (the term "conservative
model" is used only in this sense).

**(d) Closed and exact force fields.** A **time- and velocity-independent
configuration-space force field** is a $C^{1}$ map
$\varphi=(\varphi_{1},\dots,\varphi_{N}):Q\to(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$, where
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ is the open configuration domain and each
$\varphi_i(x)$ is the force on label $i$ at configuration $x$; its components
have force dimension. It represents a force map of the form
$F_i(t,x,v)=\varphi_i(x)$ on the model's state domain. This configuration-space
field is not in general an external single-label force: to identify its
$i$th component with an external map of [[post-cm02-interactions]] clause (i),
one must further require that it depend on $x_i$ alone, as in the declared
signature $F_i^{\mathrm{ext}}(t,x_i,v_i)$. Such a field is **closed** when
$\partial_{k}\varphi_{j}=\partial_{j}\varphi_{k}$ for all coordinate indices
$j,k\in\{0,\dots,3N-1\}$ at every point of $Q$, using the flattened
coordinate indices of [[def-closed-and-exact-c1-vector-fields]], and **exact with potential
energy $U$** when $\varphi=-\nabla U$ for a $C^{2}$ function

of [[def-closed-and-exact-c1-vector-fields]] with potential $U$. The following

for an open interval $J_0\subseteq(0,\infty)$
([[def-cm01-configuration]]). Suppose the model presents its force map
through the time-independent potential
$$U(x_1,x_2):=u(\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert),$$
where $u:J_0\to\mathbb R$ is of class $C^2$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), so that
$F_i(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_i}U(x)$ on the state domain ([[post-cm02-interactions]],
clauses (iii) and (iv), [[lem-cm05-radial-potential-gradient]]). Let
$x:J\to Q$ be a **motion** of the model on an interval $J$ with nonempty
interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]) and write
$$M:=m_1+m_2,\quad \mu:=\frac{m_1m_2}{M},\quad X:=\frac{m_1x_1+m_2x_2}{M},\quad V:=X',\quad P:=m_1x_1'+m_2x_2',\quad r:=x_1-x_2,$$
with $\lvert\cdot\rvert=\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ the Euclidean norm
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]) and dimensions as in [[def-cm01-units]]
($[M]=[\mu]=\mu$, $[X]=[r]=\ell$, $[P]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$). Then:

1. **(Pair forces.)** On $J$ the evaluated forces are
   $$F_1\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)=-\frac{u'(\lvert r\rvert)}{\lvert r\rvert}\,r,\qquad F_2\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)=+\frac{u'(\lvert r\rvert)}{\lvert r\rvert}\,r;$$
   thus the force map admits the external-plus-pair decomposition of
   [[post-cm02-interactions]] clause (i) with
   $F_i^{\mathrm{ext}}\equiv0$ and the single pair force
   $F_{12}=-u'(\lvert r\rvert)r/\lvert r\rvert=-F_{21}$, which is central
   and antisymmetric in the sense of clause (ii). This identity does not
   assert that a separate decomposition was declared as model data.
2. **(Centre of mass.)** $P$ is constant on $J$ and $X$ is affine: for all
   $t,t_0\in J$, $X(t)=X(t_0)+(t-t_0)V$ with the constant
   $V=X'=M^{-1}P$.
3. **(Relative motion.)** $r$ is of class $C^2$ on $J$, satisfies
   $$\mu\,r''(t)=-\frac{u'(\lvert r(t)\rvert)}{\lvert r(t)\rvert}\,r(t)\qquad(t\in J),$$
   and is therefore a **central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$** in the
   sense of [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]]; its angular momentum vector
   $j=\mu\,r\times r'$ and energy $E=\tfrac12\mu\lVert r'\rVert_2^2+
   u(\lvert r\rvert)$ are the attached objects of that definition.
4. **(Reconstruction and bijection.)** The identities
   $x_1=X+\frac{m_2}{M}r$ and $x_2=X-\frac{m_1}{M}r$ hold on $J$.
   Conversely, if $X^{\circ}:J\to\mathbb R^3$ is affine with
   $(X^{\circ})''=0$ and $r^{\circ}:J\to\mathbb R^3$ is a $C^2$ curve with
   $\lvert r^{\circ}(t)\rvert\in J_0$ and
   $\mu(r^{\circ})''=-u'(\lvert r^{\circ}\rvert)r^{\circ}/\lvert r^{\circ}\rvert$
   on $J$, then
   $$x_1^{\circ}:=X^{\circ}+\frac{m_2}{M}r^{\circ},\qquad x_2^{\circ}:=X^{\circ}-\frac{m_1}{M}r^{\circ}$$
   define a motion $x^{\circ}:J\to Q$ of the model whose centre of mass is
   $X^{\circ}$ and whose relative coordinate is $r^{\circ}$. Consequently
   the assignment $x\mapsto(X,r)$ is a bijection from the motions of the
   model on $J$ onto the pairs (affine curve $X^{\circ}$ with
   $(X^{\circ})''=0$\!, central-force trajectory $r^{\circ}$ for $(\mu,u)$
   with values in $J_0$) on $J$.
